articles.title: Brand New Layouts Achievable with CSS Subgrid
articles.description: An excellent new tutorial priming us on the possibilities unlocked by subgrid (now supported in all major browsers). As Josh noted over on Bluesky he “figured it’d be a convenient little utility” but found subgrid solves “one of the most longstanding issues” he had with CSS, and unlocks a lot of exciting UI options.
articles.author: Josh W. Comeau

articles.title: Wikipedia: Unifying Mobile and Desktop Domains
articles.description: Some detail on how a giant such as Wikipedia handles a domain change, achieving 20% faster mobile response times, improved SEO, and reduced infrastructure load as a result.
articles.author: Timo Tijhof (Wikimedia Foundation)

articles.title: Range Syntax for Style Queries
articles.description: Style queries are getting an upgrade! Una explains how, like media queries, and container queries, they can now respond to a range of values, and not just predefined states. There’s a demo at the end too.
articles.author: Una Kravets

articles.title: On Inheriting and Sharing Property Values
articles.description: A look at how CSS inheritance and computed values work, and why sharing values between properties is often difficult. Daniel also suggests a hypothetical compute() function that would let us directly get the values of other properties.
articles.author: Daniel Schwarz

articles.title: Keyframes Tokens: Standardizing Animation Across Projects
articles.description: A detailed tutorial on using a systemized approach to animation: “animations deserve the same care and structure we already give to colors, typography, and spacing”.
articles.author: Amit Sheen

articles.title: How to Create 3D Images in CSS with the Layered Pattern
articles.description: A fun one here on creating 3D objects using the CSS perspective and transform properties.
articles.author: Sunkanmi Fafowora

articles.title: How grid-template-areas Offer a Visual Solution for Your Code
articles.description: A quick look at how to make use of this flexible property to help with layout design.
articles.author: Saron Yitbarek (WebKit)

articles.title: Web Monetization is Still Inching Along, But Still Too Difficult
articles.description: A sound idea, but one that no one has cracked just yet.
articles.author: Chris Coyier

articles.title: Driver.js v1.4: Tours, Highlights, Contextual Help, and More
articles.description: A vanilla JS library for making on-page tours and contextual help systems. It’s been around for several years, but is still maintained, and there are lots of examples to check out – it’s really smooth.
articles.author: Kamran Ahmed

articles.title: Awesome Tailwind CSS: Awesome Things Related to Tailwind
articles.description: A grab bag of handy links, tools, plugins, and utilities.
articles.author: NiftyCo

articles.title: wc-pagination: A Web Component for Accessible Pagination
articles.description: Relies on three attributes to determine the number of items per page, current page, and total items. Try some demos on CodePen here.
articles.author: Dominic Myers

articles.title: Heat.js: A Heat Map Visualization Library
articles.description: Think the GitHub contributions heat map. No dependencies, small, responsive, and theme-able. There’s a live demo or its GitHub repo.
articles.author: William Troup

articles.title: Polypane 27: Projects, A Snippets Panel and Chromium 142
articles.description: The latest version of developer browser Polypane brings a new project-focused workflow, a new snippets panel, and improved DOM editing.
articles.author: Kilian Valkhof

articles.title: fontless: Plug-and-Play Font Optimization for Modern Web Apps
articles.description: A Vite plugin that lets you use fonts as you normally would. It will optimize font loading by providing fallbacks for reduced Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). No JS required at runtime and works with any framework.
articles.author: fontaine

articles.title: Fran Sans Essay
articles.description: I enjoyed this write up covering the inspiration, design and creation of a new display font. It’s based on the LCD displays found on San Francisco’s Muni.
articles.author: Emily Sneddon
